title: The history of the language and the release cycle

videos.script: Lesson 1 said why Go was made. This lesson follows it from 2009 to the release on your machine. {{timeline}} Go became public in November 2009, and Go 1 arrived in 2012. Every release since then has been Go 1 point something. The number counts releases of one language, not new languages. {{promise}} Go 1 came with a promise: a program that works today keeps working. You will test that promise with one small program. The same loop prints two different answers, and the only thing you change is one line of go.mod. {{calendar}} Then the calendar. A new Go arrives twice a year, in February and in August, and you read the dates straight from the module proxy. Each one gets fixes until two newer ones exist, which is about a year. {{toolchain}} Last, the go command fetching a different Go by itself, because go.mod asked for it. By the end you can read a go.mod and say which Go it needs, and what happens when you do not have it.
